evidence.claim: memory model looks tiny or packed
evidence.detail: no relocations at all: either a single-segment program or a packed one

Two very different programs look like this: hand-written assembly, and C built by a compiler that omits frame pointers under optimisation (Open Watcom does, Microsoft C 5.x does not). Tell them apart by running libsig.py with each shipped database -- a compiled program will match a C runtime, assembly will not. Either way, expect function boundary recovery to miss more than the measured figures suggest.

limitations: The memory model is inferred from how many relocations there are and where they sit, not read from the file; a program that builds its segment values at run time looks smaller than it is.
Packers are recognised by signature, and EXEPACK by its 'RB' marker. A packer with no signature in triage.py's table is not detected; few relocations with few stack frames is the only other hint.

Stack frames are counted as the bytes 55 8B EC anywhere in the load image, without disassembling. The other encoding of mov bp,sp (89 E5) and ENTER are not counted, and the same bytes inside data are.
Interpreted engines are recognised by engine names in the binary and by the size of the files beside it. An engine that names nothing and keeps its data elsewhere passes as an ordinary program.

Two very different programs look like this: hand-written assembly, and C built by a compiler that omits frame pointers under optimisation (Open Watcom does, Microsoft C 5.x does not). Tell them apart by running libsig.py with each shipped database -- a compiled program will match a C runtime, assembly will not. Either way, expect function boundary recovery to miss more than the measured figures suggest.

evidence.detail: Overlaid code is swapped into a shared region, so several functions occupy the same addresses at different times. Nothing here handles that; each overlay needs its own address space.

limitations: The memory model is inferred from how many relocations there are and where they sit, not read from the file; a program that builds its segment values at run time looks smaller than it is.
Packers are recognised by signature, and EXEPACK by its 'RB' marker. A packer with no signature in triage.py's table is not detected; few relocations with few stack frames is the only other hint.

Stack frames are counted as the bytes 55 8B EC anywhere in the load image, without disassembling. The other encoding of mov bp,sp (89 E5) and ENTER are not counted, and the same bytes inside data are.
Interpreted engines are recognised by engine names in the binary and by the size of the files beside it. An engine that names nothing and keeps its data elsewhere passes as an ordinary program.
